calibration_rulings.title: The red-bread sentence «یہ “لال روٹی” (خبز احمر) بھی کہلاتی ہے۔»: the Urdu-script transliteration, the marks, and «لال» or «سرخ».
calibration_rulings.binds: food.g0.d7.pre; the entry «خبز احمر»; the C5b pair.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: «یہ “لال روٹی” (خبز احمر) بھی کہلاتی ہے۔» — the alias both sources quote, in marks (N72, N113), in the English’s order, the transliteration the English carries written in Urdu script from the Arabic «الخبز الأحمر» (article dropped, N284; P11), as the three earlier lines kept theirs; «لال» over «سرخ» (the everyday colour word of the kitchen). The naming verb «کہلاتی» is feminine by «روٹی» (N107/N170 frame). The on-05 reader understood both as names of one bread (item 24); the bracket’s purpose unsignalled is minor. C («“خبز احمر” (لال روٹی)») stays on record as the fallback; B drops a name the English carries; D («سرخ») not taken. C5b SYNONYM_PAIRS (coordinator, after stage 7): «کھجور کی روٹی» ↔ «لال روٹی». ROUND 2: Both readers read the marks as an alternative name; both found the bracket unsignalled (minor). A stands. ‖ AMENDED b20-ui (owner decision 2026-10-15): B, by the owner’s decision of 2026-10-15: «یہ “لال روٹی” بھی کہلاتی ہے۔» — the alias both sources quote, in marks (N72, N113), «لال» over «سرخ» and the feminine naming verb «کہلاتی» as A ruled; the bracket «(خبز احمر)» leaves with the English transliteration. The entry «خبز احمر» no longer stands on /ur/ (kept for search). C5b SYNONYM_PAIRS unchanged: «کھجور کی روٹی» ↔ «لال روٹی». Confirmed in place (on-05 item 17).
calibration_rulings.guard: Stage checker: the string «“لال روٹی” (خبز احمر)» does not occur. For the proofreader, not machine-read: the date-bread card carries «یہ “لال روٹی” بھی کہلاتی ہے۔» once, in its naming clause. The machine clause bans the withdrawn bracketed wording only.
calibration_rulings.ruled_by: Judge round2, b19-ui (round 4), 2026-10-15; owner decided 2026-10-15, carried by the b20-ui judge, round 1

calibration_rulings.title: methodP2 without the loan «کارڈ»: «اس صفحے کے چار پکوانوں کے تعارف میں» — does it still say that four CARDS mention the occasions?
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: «اس صفحے کے چار پکوانوں کے تعارف میں …» — the count kept, the mention placed in each dish’s introduction; no loan. The on-05 reader tied the sentence to four of the dishes (item 27); his difficulty in matching four occasions to four dishes is the source’s (logged). Round 1 gives the next sentence the plural that points back to the four («ان پکوانوں», change 7). B stays the fallback; C («کارڈ») refused under P16. ROUND 2: The on-r1 reader charged the note’s register and the unnamed four dishes (item 28): the source’s; A stands. ‖ AMENDED b20-ui (owner decision 2026-10-15): A stands, in the owner’s order: «الاحساء کی کھانے پینے کی جگہوں میں یہ پکوان سال بھر پیش کیے جاتے ہیں۔ اس صفحے کے چار پکوانوں کے تعارف میں کسی موقع یا موسم کا ذکر آیا ہے، یعنی رمضان، سردیوں کی راتیں، شادی کی دعوتیں اور مہمان نوازی کے دسترخوان۔ یہ ذکر …». The count and the four occasions exactly (owner). The register of A’s two sentences, charged by the on-05 reader of b20-ui, is recorded for the owner: rewording them is outside a reorder.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: methodP2 opens on the all-year sentence and keeps «چار» and the four occasions; «کارڈ» is not written.
calibration_rulings.ruled_by: Judge round2, b19-ui (round 4), 2026-10-15; owner decided 2026-10-15 (order), carried by the b20-ui judge, round 1

calibration_rulings.title: food.dineCta leads to the ENGLISH restaurants index: should the Urdu label say so?
calibration_rulings.binds: food.dineCta; every /ur/ link to a page that has no Urdu version yet.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: «یہ پکوان کہاں چکھیں؟ کھانے پینے کی جگہیں دیکھیں ←», no language note: the note is not in the source string, the Russian line that faced the same English target added none, and the approved Urdu links do not mark English targets. The on-05 reader found the link clear, natural and useful (item 30); he did not follow it. FOR THE COORDINATOR / OWNER, one line: the link opens the English restaurants index; a site-wide marker for English targets on /ur/ (e.g. «(انگریزی میں)») is a decision for the whole interface, not this string. ROUND 2: CONFIRMED by both readers (on-r1 item 30). ‖ AMENDED b20-ui (owner decision 2026-10-15): A, CLOSED by the owner on 2026-10-15: «یہ پکوان کہاں چکھیں؟ کھانے پینے کی جگہیں دیکھیں ←», no language note; no marker for English targets anywhere on /ur/ links. Nothing for the coordinator beyond entering the closure.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: a /ur/ link to an English page carries no language note; the dineCta label is the approved «کھانے پینے کی جگہیں» with the arrow «←».

calibration_rulings.title: Tomato sauce in the rice card: «ٹماٹر کی چٹنی» — the on-05 reader pictured a chutney cooked into the rice (item 5, moderate); stage 5 reported «ٹماٹر» as an English-origin word without a termbase entry (checklist item 9).
calibration_rulings.ruling: C (round 2): the rice card names «ٹماٹر» alone — «… گوشت یا مرغی، ٹماٹر اور مسالوں (…) کے ساتھ …». Two readers of two read «ٹماٹر کی چٹنی» (round 1’s A) as the side chutney, and the reference’s own article defines it so: a misreading of what goes into the dish outweighs the loss of the form ’sauce’, which is charged under accuracy. B refused under P16 (no entry; a native wording exists); D refused: «مسالا» beside «مسالوں» in the same list reads as the spices. «ٹماٹر» is an English loan with its own Urdu headword and gender (Rekhta, Origin English, Noun Masculine) and no native competitor: P16 is satisfied by the headword, as N126 ruled for «کیتلی»; entered verified as «ٹماٹر» (addendum to round 2). Round 1’s pending entry «ٹماٹر کی چٹنی» is withdrawn (never in the termbase); a real tomato chutney on a later page is still «ٹماٹر کی چٹنی». ‖ AMENDED b20-ui (judge record correction 2026-10-15): C (round 2): the rice card names «ٹماٹر» alone — «… گوشت یا مرغی، ٹماٹر اور مسالوں (…) کے ساتھ …». Two readers of two read «ٹماٹر کی چٹنی» (round 1’s A) as the side chutney, and the reference’s own article defines it so: a misreading of what goes into the dish outweighs the loss of the form ’sauce’, which is charged under accuracy. B refused under P16 (no entry; a native wording exists); D refused: «مسالا» beside «مسالوں» in the same list reads as the spices. «ٹماٹر» is the naturalised everyday word, not a P16 admission. Round 1’s pending entry «ٹماٹر کی چٹنی» is withdrawn (never in the termbase). CARRIED by the b20-ui judge, round 2 (proof on r1, should-fix 1): the addendum’s wording, so that the checker reads the scoped guard from a judge-round file.
calibration_rulings.guard: Stage checker: the string «ٹماٹر کی چٹنی اور مسالوں» does not occur. For the proofreader, not machine-read: tomato sauce cooked into a dish is «ٹماٹر»; «ساس», «پیسٹ», «گریوی» are not written; a tomato chutney served on the side is still «ٹماٹر کی چٹنی».
calibration_rulings.ruled_by: Judge round 1, b19-ui (round 4), 2026-10-15; amended by Judge round 2, b19-ui (round 4), 2026-10-15; record corrected by the judge’s addendum to that round; carried by the b20-ui judge, round 2

calibration_rulings.title: An image of the source that the Urdu renders with a fixed phrase of another sense, or literally enough to mislead: mandi ’not so much cooked as entrusted to the earth, the way secrets are’ (AR «لا يُطهى … بل يُستودَع في باطن الأرض كما تُستودَع الأسرار»).
calibration_rulings.binds: food.g0.d1.pre; any later figure of the source whose literal Urdu is a fixed idiom of another sense.
calibration_rulings.ruling: D (round 2): the image stays; no wording of it reads as burial or as undercooking. (1) Where an Urdu fixed phrase carries a sense the source’s image does not (burial: «زمین کے سپرد», «امانت» in the earth), the image is said in the source’s own terms — the Arabic’s, the authority: in the depth of the earth, kept as a secret is kept. (2) Where the literal form of a contrast measures what the source only ranks (’not so much cooked as’ → «پکایا کم جاتا ہے», read as ’little cooked’), the contrast ranks: «پکانے سے بڑھ کر». The verb is «سنبھال کر رکھنا» (to keep with care, the frame of a secret kept); the ’trust’ nuance of «يُستودَع» is what leaves, charged under accuracy. A and B are withdrawn; C refused (adding information; the method is logged as the source’s). D is unread until the r2 blind read. ‖ AMENDED b20-ui (owner decision 2026-10-15): D stands with the owner’s plain sentence after it: «… جیسے راز سنبھال کر رکھے جاتے ہیں۔ سادہ لفظوں میں، یہ پکوان زمین کے ایک گڑھے میں دبے ہوئے تندور میں پکتا ہے۔». The plain sentence does its job (the reader learned the method from it); the figure, kept by the owner, still misleads when read first — logged for the owner (source_defects 1), not reworded on a reader’s charge. The rest of D’s ruling (the image said in the source’s own terms; the contrast ranks) stands; C of b19 (a plain method) is now the source’s own sentence, not an addition.
calibration_rulings.guard: Stage checker: none of «زمین کے سپرد زیادہ», «میں امانت زیادہ رکھا», «راز امانت رکھے», «پکایا کم جاتا ہے» occurs. For the proofreader, not machine-read: the mandi figure keeps the source’s ranking and is followed by the plain sentence of the method, which states only a tannour, buried, in a pit in the ground; the tannour is not said to be buried with a word of human burial. The machine clause bans the withdrawn wordings of this one image, not the words «امانت» or «تہہ» elsewhere.
calibration_rulings.ruled_by: Judge round2, b19-ui (round 4), 2026-10-15; record corrected by the judge’s addendum to that round; owner decided 2026-10-15 (the plain sentence), carried by the b20-ui judge, round 1; guard narrowed by the b20-ui judge, round 2 (proof on r1, should-fix 2)

calibration_rulings.title: The Hasawi rice dish name (EN “Hasawi Rice”, AR «الأرز الأحسائي»), reopened by the owner on 2026-10-15 for a clearer Urdu DISH name than «الاحساء کے چاول», one name byte-identical on the card, its photo text, the meta description and cat.taste.d.
calibration_rulings.binds: food.g0.d0.name, food.g0.d0.alt, food.g0.d0.pre (its closing anaphor), food.description, cat.taste.d; the entry «پلاؤ»; every later interface string that names this dish.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: «الاحساء کا پلاؤ» (masculine singular) — food.g0.d0.name, the alt «لکڑیوں کی آگ پر مٹی کی ہانڈی میں چلایا جا رہا الاحساء کا پلاؤ», food.description and cat.taste.d, byte for byte; the closing sentence of food.g0.d0.pre refers back by the head noun, «یہ پلاؤ … پیش کیا جاتا ہے», as approved_today did («یہ چاول»). «پلاؤ» is the Urdu dictionary word for what the card describes (Rekhta: Persian, Noun, Masculine, “a dish of spiced rice with meat or vegetables”), Urdu names a regional rice dish place + dish word (کابلی پلاؤ, سندھی پلاؤ), and N115 / N281 set the place as the head name with the possessive. Confirmed in place by the blind reader (items 5, 25). COST, charged under accuracy: both sources say “rice”; «پلاؤ» names the dish by its class, which the card’s own description states. B refused: five words in a heading and in two lists, and it still opens on «الاحساء کے چاول…», the grain parse the owner asked to remove. C refused: the owner’s “adjectival form” was an example in his request for candidates, not a decision against N115 / N281, and «احسائی» is attested only in personal names (ur.wikipedia 41 pages, all persons). The local GRAIN named as an ingredient («الاحساء کے مقامی چاول», d0.pre and heroSum) is not the dish name and stays.
calibration_rulings.guard: Stage checker: none of «الاحساء کے چاول، ہریس», «الاحساء کے چاول، مندی», «چلائے جا رہے الاحساء کے چاول», «یہ چاول تقریبات میں» occurs. For the proofreader, not machine-read: the rice card name is «الاحساء کا پلاؤ», byte-identical in its alt, the meta description and cat.taste.d; the grain as an ingredient («الاحساء کے مقامی چاول») is a different phrase and stays where the source names the grain; no Urdu adjective of Al-Ahsa (N115, N281). The machine clause bans the four withdrawn wordings of this dish name only, never the phrase for the grain.
